# Independent terminal metadata audit

The stored terminal packet is internally consistent. I did not author
`terminal-01`; this is an independent read-only audit of its retained files,
not a fresh GitHub/CI execution or a release result. No network request,
fixture driver, recorded log command, Rust/Lean build/test, Qleisli CLI/native
process or Git/GitHub mutation was performed. Only this additive directory
was written.

The required constitutional startup was completed before packet-dependent
work. `python3 scripts/check_constitution.py --base-ref
faa5cfb5e7ea1cf3b39a43b80f7f2345e89197c2` exited 0. Its identity check does
not authenticate the human transcript or replay Lean. The two protected
ordinary QLV1 ownership/scope guarantees remain limited to their admitted
premises; broader QS/PR/RS and EXACT duties remain pending.

All 26 terminal members declared by `files.json` match their SHA-256, byte
count and mode; that self-excluded map is separately pinned here. The
inventory was exact before adding this audit. All 19 referenced historical
files match both preserved before/after maps and their current bytes/modes.
The tested workflow is byte-identical to its historical copy. Original
terminal and historical records were rechecked after writing this audit.

All 17 gzip logs decompress with valid gzip CRC/length and exact UTF-8
round-trip. Their 2,071,956 decoded bytes match every stored connector raw
identity. Six reused historical logs also match their historical compressed
and decoded identities; the eleven new gzip files total 137,519 bytes and
have zero header mtime. This binds the retained connector-decoded text,
including original whitespace/BOM/ANSI bytes, rather than original HTTP ZIP
bytes or downloaded CI artifacts. A local file audit cannot independently
re-establish the claimed network fetch provenance.

Both jobs sources agree on all 18 IDs, names and conclusions, and on every
executed step projection. The full API metadata matches recorded completion
times and all 24 skipped steps. Seventeen jobs succeeded; release-readiness
111932055584 was skipped with no executed steps. The sole representation
difference is `steps=[]` in the API versus `steps=null` in the connector for
that skipped job. My initial literal comparison failed on that difference;
the actual failure and explicitly bounded correction are preserved in
`audit.json`. This was an audit assertion failure, not a CI failure.

Every one of the 17 stored checkout logs binds tested merge
`7549cecca246b9335a3e1b8f9e4a176df8827d0a`. The eight required gates bind the
same merge and selected `full/full` validation, with all eight producer
results successful. Stored run/job metadata names published head
`9256fe9ef4ffa722066b0569ee37341cf65dea0d`; the merge projection gives ordered
parents `ba83c5c97a9c67bf3904423745b3e9c019a083cb`, then that head. Its tree
matches the stored run head tree. All selected checkout/gate/result line
numbers and complete ignored-test rows match the actual decompressed logs.
The merge file is honestly an API metadata projection omitting 300 changed
file rows, rather than a complete HTTP response.

README scope matches the stored workflow, steps and logs: full kernel
reduction/fresh replay, native comparisons, relocated Linux/macOS full
bundle checks (267 process checks and 84 small corpus clients each), schema
rebinding and registered guarantee replay succeeded. The model-only proof
compile step was skipped under `full`; full replay was not skipped. Each
Rust producer retains 52 per-command ignored test rows, which are not a
global list of untested features. All 16 producer receipt/upload steps,
seven required uploads and the model-only compile account for the 24 step
skips. The docs required context retained the shared report. The original
metadata-audit failure and correction are preserved and are not a CI
failure.

This evidence covers that historical tested merge. It does not validate
later common frontend/Formals edits or local commit
`7e04f20f0c908fd56720a50655bc56c072c80ceb`, downloaded release artifacts,
release readiness, adoption, new guarantees, broader theorem discharge,
source/runtime preservation, Issue completion or publication. The original
packet makes none of those claims. No actionable mismatch was found within
the declared stored-data scope.
